motions.motion: Councilmember Burnham moved to approve the Consent Agenda removing Items 10.A, 11.B., and 11.C., and placing them on the scheduled items for further discussion. Councilmember Gray seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Consent agenda approved, three items pulled
motions.summary: The council approved its consent agenda after pulling three items out of the bundle for separate discussion later in the meeting.
motions.impact: Nothing changes for residents — this is the batch of routine items the council passes in a single vote, with the three pulled items taken up on their own.

motions.item_title: Table the McDonald's (City Center) Site Plan to require completion of a traffic study prior to…
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to table the McDonald's (City Center) Site Plan to require completion of a traffic study prior to approval. Councilmember Wright seconded the motion.
motions.headline: McDonald's plan paused for a traffic study
motions.summary: The council put the McDonald's site plan at City Center on hold until a traffic study is completed.
motions.impact: The City Center McDonald's cannot be approved until traffic near the site is studied, so the project is pushed back. Nothing changes on the ground in the meantime.

motions.item_title: A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Expressing an Intent to Work in Partnership with the West Traverse Sentinel Landscape (WTSL) Committee for the Relocation of the Eagle Mountain City Rodeo Grounds within the Army Compatible Use Buffer (ACUB) Area Surrounding Camp Williams
motions.motion: Councilmember Wright moved to adopt a Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Expressing an Intent to Work in Partnership with the West Traverse Sentinel Landscape (WTSL) Committee for the Relocation of the Eagle Mountain City Eagle Mountain City Council Agenda – April 15, 2025 Page 6 of 13 Rodeo Grounds within the Army Compatible Use Buffer (ACUB) Area Surrounding Camp Williams. Councilmember Clark seconded the motion.
motions.outcome: passed with a unanimous vote of 4:0.
motions.headline: City backs moving the rodeo grounds
motions.summary: The council declared its intent to work with the West Traverse Sentinel Landscape committee on relocating the city rodeo grounds into the buffer area around Camp Williams.
motions.impact: Nothing moves yet — this only commits the city to work with the partner group on a possible new site. If you use the rodeo grounds, expect a relocation plan to come back for a real decision later.

motions.item_title: A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving the Fee Reduction Request of Brett Simpson for a Master Development Plan Amendment Application from $3,350 to $1,350
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to waive the fee for Brett Simpson’s Gazelle Run Master Development Plan Amendment Application. Councilmember Gray seconded the motion. Councilmembers sought clarification on the intended use of the fee and collectively expressed that the fee should be reduced rather than fully waived. AMENDED MOTION: Councilmember Wood moved to adopt a Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving the Fee Reduction Request of Brett Simpson for a Master Development Plan Amendment Application from $3,350 to $1,350. Councilmember Gray seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Gazelle Run application fee cut to $1,350
motions.summary: The council cut the fee for Brett Simpson's Gazelle Run master development plan amendment from $3,350 to $1,350, rather than waiving it entirely as first proposed.
motions.impact: This touches one applicant only. The city collects $2,000 less on this single application, and the fees everyone else pays are unchanged.

motions.item_title: A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) Projects for the Fiscal Year 2026 as follows: • PUBLIC SERVICE PROJECTS: o LMI Cemetery Services Assistance - $5,000 o LMI Utility Assistance - $15,000 o Senior Assistance Program - $3,000 o LMI Back-to-School Drive - $5,000 o Tabitha’s Way Food Pantry - $7,292 ▪ TOTALS: $35,292 • OTHER PROJECTS: o LMI Yard Cleanup - $36,163.20 o ADA Ramp/Crosswalk Installation at Fiona St/Airport Rd - $20,000 o Small Business Grants - $150,000 • TOTALS: $206,163.20 Councilmember Burnham seconded the motion
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to adopt a Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) Projects for the Fiscal Year 2026 as follows: • PUBLIC SERVICE PROJECTS: o LMI Cemetery Services Assistance - $5,000 o LMI Utility Assistance - $15,000 o Senior Assistance Program - $3,000 o LMI Back-to-School Drive - $5,000 o Tabitha’s Way Food Pantry - $7,292 ▪ TOTALS: $35,292 • OTHER PROJECTS: o LMI Yard Cleanup - $36,163.20 o ADA Ramp/Crosswalk Installation at Fiona St/Airport Rd - $20,000 o Small Business Grants - $150,000 • TOTALS: $206,163.20 Councilmember Burnham seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Block grant money set: $150K for small businesses
motions.summary: The city set its 2026 federal block grant spending: $150,000 in small business grants, $36,163 for yard cleanup, $20,000 for an ADA crosswalk, and $35,292 in aid programs.
motions.impact: Small businesses can apply for grant money, and lower-income households get help with utility bills, cemetery costs, school supplies, food and yard cleanup. A new ADA ramp and crosswalk is funded at Fiona Street and Airport Road.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the General Plan Future Land Use Map for Certain Lands Known as Cedar Valley Holbrook
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to table an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the General Plan Future Land Use Map for Certain Lands Known as Cedar Valley Holbrook. Councilmember Wright seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Cedar Valley Holbrook land use change delayed
motions.summary: The council delayed a decision on changing the long-range land use map for the land known as Cedar Valley Holbrook.
motions.impact: Nothing changes — this map change was set aside along with the related rezoning and will return to the council later.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Rezoning Certain Lands Known as Cedar Valley Holbrook
motions.motion: Councilmember Burnham moved to table an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Rezoning Certain Lands Known as Cedar Valley Holbrook. Councilmember Wright seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Cedar Valley Holbrook rezoning put on hold
motions.summary: The council delayed a decision on rezoning the land known as Cedar Valley Holbrook.
motions.impact: Nothing changes for now. The proposal is set aside and has to come back to the council before anything about that land is decided.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the General Plan Future Land Use Map for Certain Lands Known as Cedar Corners Phase 5 from Neighborhood Residential 1 to Neighborhood Residential 2
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to adopt an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the General Plan Future Land Use Map for Certain Lands Known as Cedar Corners Phase 5 from Neighborhood Residential 1 to Neighborhood Residential 2. Councilmember Burnham seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Land use map updated for Cedar Corners Phase 5
motions.summary: The council changed the city's long-range land use map for Cedar Corners Phase 5 from Neighborhood Residential 1 to Neighborhood Residential 2.
motions.impact: This updates the city's long-term plan for that land so it matches the rezoning approved the same night. Nothing changes anywhere else in the city.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Rezoning Certain Lands Known as Cedar Corners Phase 5 from Residential to RC Zone
motions.motion: Councilmember Wright moved to adopt an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Rezoning Certain Lands Known as Cedar Corners Phase 5 from Residential to RC Zone. Councilmember Wood seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Cedar Corners Phase 5 rezoned to RC
motions.summary: The council changed the zoning on the Cedar Corners Phase 5 land from residential to the city's RC zone.
motions.impact: This is the zoning step behind the Cedar Corners Phase 5 project. If you live nearby, what can be built on that land is now governed by RC zone rules instead of the old residential rules.

motions.item_title: A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving the Cedar Corners Phase 5 Development Agreement
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to adopt a Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving the Cedar Corners Phase 5 Development Agreement with the following additions: 1. That the applicant work with Planning staff on establishing a benchmark for when construction can be started; 2. That the pedestrian rights of way are connecting, and the two roads are connecting on either side of Poplar Drive and Maple Street. Councilmember Wright seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Cedar Corners Phase 5 development deal approved
motions.summary: The city approved a development agreement for Cedar Corners Phase 5, with conditions on when construction may start and on connecting the roads and sidewalks.
motions.impact: If you live near Poplar Drive or Maple Street, the developer must connect the roads on both sides and keep the walkways continuous rather than leaving them to dead-end.
